title: Minimizing Coins
explanation: Unbounded coins with arbitrary values: dp[s] = 1 + min dp[s − c]. Greedy fails for arbitrary coin systems.
traps: Unreachable sums must stay at ∞, not 0.
Greedy (largest coin first) fails, e.g. coins {1, 3, 4}, x = 6.

extraLayers.prompt: What should the DP state represent?

options.text: dp[s] = minimum number of coins whose values sum to exactly s
dp[i][s] = minimum coins using only coin i for sum s
options.why: Coins can be mixed; restricting to one coin type is wrong.

options.text: dp[s] = number of ways to make s
options.why: Counts ways instead of minimizing the number of coins.

options.text: dp[c] = how many times coin c is used
options.why: That's an answer description, not a subproblem.

extraLayers.explanation: Every sum s is a subproblem; the best way to pay s ends with some coin c.

extraLayers.prompt: Given that state, which transition is right?

options.text: dp[s] = 1 + min over coins c ≤ s of dp[s − c]; dp[0] = 0; unreachable = ∞

options.why: That's greedy; it fails for coin systems like {1, 3, 4}.

options.text: dp[s] = Σ over coins c of dp[s − c]
options.why: Sums ways; you want a minimum.

options.text: dp[s] = min over coins c of dp[s − c]
options.why: Forgets to count the coin you just used (+1).

extraLayers.explanation: Try every coin as the last one paid and keep the best.
